# Riftblood

Some sorcerers trace their power to dragons. Others to wild magic, or storms, or divine bloodlines. Riftblood sorcerers trace theirs to a Rift surge — a cascade of violet-black energy that swept through their birthplace, their mother's womb, or their own body at the moment of birth.

The Rift is in their blood. It leaks when they cast. It whispers when they sleep. It bends probability around them without asking permission. They didn't choose this. But they've learned to use it.

## Rift Surge

*1st-level Riftblood feature*

Your magic carries the Rift's instability. Immediately after you cast a sorcerer spell of 1st level or higher, the DM can have you roll a d20. On a 1, roll on the Rift Surge table to create a random magical effect. Rift Surges can only occur once per turn.

If a Rift Surge has an effect that requires a saving throw, the DC equals your spell save DC.

## Tides of the Veil

*1st-level Riftblood feature*

You can manipulate the Rift's distortion of probability. When you make an attack roll, ability check, or saving throw, you can give yourself advantage on the roll. You can do so before or after rolling, but before the outcome is determined.

Once you use this feature, you cannot use it again until you finish a long rest. However, any time before you regain the use of this feature, the DM can have you roll on the Rift Surge table immediately after you cast a sorcerer spell of 1st level or higher — no d20 required. You then regain the use of Tides of the Veil.

## Veil Bend

*6th-level Riftblood feature*

The Rift distorts probability around you — and now you can direct that distortion. When a creature within 60 feet of you makes an attack roll, ability check, or saving throw, you can use your reaction and spend 2 sorcery points to roll 1d4 and apply the result as a bonus or penalty (your choice) to the creature's roll. You can do so after the creature rolls but before the outcome is determined.

The Veil flickers. The odds shift. The Riftmeddles.

## Controlled Rift

*14th-level Riftblood feature*

You've learned to guide the Rift's chaos, if not quite control it. When you roll on the Rift Surge table, you can roll twice and use either result. The Rift knows its own — and it's less likely to hurt you than it used to be.

## Rift Bombardment

*18th-level Riftblood feature*

The Rift amplifies your peaks. When you roll damage for a sorcerer spell and any of the damage dice show their maximum result, you can roll one additional damage die and add it to the total. You can use this feature only once per turn.

When your magic peaks, the Rift pushes it higher.
